appraisal_events.evidence: quand M. Verdurin avait dit que Swann ne lui revenait pas... il avait deviné celle de sa femme; ils avaient très vite senti en lui un espace réservé, impénétrable... une impossibilité de les lui imposer, de l'y convertir entièrement; ... précipita la disgrâce de Swann
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explains that despite loving the Verdurins more than any other faithful, Swann falls into open disgrace because his inner independence resists full absorption into the clan's dogmas, a resistance they cannot forgive.

appraisal_events.evidence: Quelle différence avec un « nouveau »... sur lequel ils fondaient beaucoup d'espoir... fit ressortir ses qualités... une gaieté dont la franchise avait charmé Mme Verdurin
appraisal_events.explanation: At his first dinner Forcheville's crude but eager conformity to the clan's tastes and jokes wins the Verdurins' hopeful favor and visibly delights Mme Verdurin, a rise the narrator frames ironically by noting Forcheville is 'grossièrement snob' and lacks Swann's delicacy.

status_effects.explanation: Swann's standing in the Verdurin milieu collapses into declared disgrace despite his greater devotion to the group than any other member.
His reserved, unconvertible inner space marks him as never fully assimilable into the clan, a lasting exclusion from full belonging despite his ostensible welcome.
Forcheville's ready conformity and appreciative gaiety charm Mme Verdurin and raise the hopes placed in him, elevating his local standing at his very first dinner.

ambiguities: Forcheville's local elevation in the Verdurins' eyes is explicitly undercut by the narrator's aside that he is 'grossièrement snob' and lacks Swann's delicacy, so the positive movement is social/local favor rather than narratorial endorsement of his character.
